Anna Liu: Quick sync — load test from last night after the KV-cache + batching tweak shows a weird tail spike for short sequences (~8-32 tokens). p95 jumps ~2.5x under light concurrency. Anyone seen this?
Kevin Patel: Do you have the exact harness? client or server-side change? keepalive settings?
Anna Liu: Server change was kernel selector tweak + dynamic batcher delay reduction. Client was our replay harness (short-lived connections by default) — not sure if it was reusing connections.
Maria Gomez: Uploading the profiler summary I grabbed while reproing. Hot stack: fused_attention_path -> fallback_attention_generic -> feed_forward. Flame shows many small samples in TLS handshake too.
Maria Gomez: ```
# perf top snapshot (abbreviated)
  fused_attention_path  28.7%
  fallback_attention_generic 17.9%
  evp_do_handshake (OpenSSL) 6.1%
  recvmsg (kernel) 4.3%
```
Samir Khan: The dynamic batching change reduced the collector delay to 1ms for small seqs which increased microbatch churn. That can reduce KV cache reuse because requests no longer land in the same batch/step. Could explain extra LM compute and cache misses.
Kevin Patel: Also client side: if your harness opens new TCP/TLS per request you add ~7-12ms per connection (handshake) + Nagle/TCP slowstart quirks. gRPC warm channel reuse avoids that. Are we comparing gRPC vs REST with identical client pooling?
Maria Gomez: This is the apples-to-apples thing: different transport/conn reuse can mask server perf regressions. For fair comparisons we need: same concurrency, same client connection reuse (keepalive or pooled gRPC channel), identical payloads, same TLS settings, and same kernel/build.
Kevin Patel: Minimal repro I used: 
```bash
# keepalive off (bad)
curl -s -H "Connection: close" https://api.redwood.local/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
# keepalive on (ok)
curl -s --http1.1 https://api.redwood.local/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
```
Observed ~9ms extra per-call when Connection: close is used.
perf-bot: Regression alert: p95 latency +140% on route /generate after merge r/4521 (kernel selector). Known issue: selector prefers generic kernel for seq<=32 when fused kernels detect shape mismatch.
Anna Liu: Action items: 1) Run replay harness with recorded arrival times (10k requests) using both connection pooling and single-request connections. 2) Re-run with kernel selector pinned to previous behavior. 3) Profile KV-hit rate and batch size distribution. 4) Compare gRPC long-lived channels vs REST keepalive. Samir/Kevin can you take 1/2?
Samir Khan: I'll run 10k replay with our harness and capture per-request: batch_size, kv_hit, kernel_choice. Will try with adaptive_delay=off and on.
Kevin Patel: I'll reproduce with both curl and grpc-client; will test TCP_NODELAY toggle, and disable TLS session resumption to see handshake impact.
Maria Gomez: When you run profiler, please also capture OpenSSL timelines (SSL_read/SSL_do_handshake) and kernel samples. If kernel_choice flips to fallback_attention_generic we probably regressed kernel selection heuristics.
Anna Liu: For measurement, report p50/p95/p99/p999, server CPU% and batch size histogram. Include the replay recording (arrival timestamps) so we can rerun. Also attach any flame graphs. :thumbsup:
Samir Khan: Ack. I'll post logs and a short gist with the harness command and flags.
Kevin Patel: One more note — when comparing gRPC vs REST, mind that HTTP/2 multiplexing can hide batching behavior because multiple streams share a connection; that changes arrival timing at the server. Use recorded arrival times to avoid that artifact.
Anna Liu: Exactly. Let's avoid conflating transport-level multiplexing with server batching heuristics. Thanks all, ping me when you have the runs.
